frequency_question: How often do high-priority, capital-subsidy and financing schemes backed by executive will and legislative capability successfully reach formal finalization and implementation within 30 months?
membership_rule: Includes central government manufacturing/transport incentive schemes announced with explicit financial outlays that required bureaucratic drafting and cabinet/ministerial sign-off; excludes minor program renewals or schemes blocked solely by legislative defeat (since majority control is given).

cases.name: FAME India Phase II (Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of Electric Vehicles)
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell Battery Storage
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Components

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 7 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 7 major comprehensive EV and manufacturing incentive packages launched by the Union Ministry of Heavy Industries / Cabinet within the last decade; 7 successfully finalized and implemented.
known_gaps: Minor sub-schemes or delayed drafts that were subsumed into larger umbrella programs rather than failing outright.
multiplier: 7 hits out of 7 major comparable initiatives executed by the Ministry of Heavy Industries and allied line ministries under continuous majority governance.
validity_reason: The institutional mechanisms, bureaucratic processing speed, and political priority attached to green mobility and manufacturing subsidies remain stable under the current administration.
